question: What actions can your agent take in our systems, and how are those permissions enforced at the moment a tool is called?
why_they_ask: The buyer stays responsible for everything that happens in its systems. An agent acting outside its intended authority is a named risk in agent frameworks, and instructions in a prompt are not an enforcement mechanism.
strong_answer: Names every tool the agent can call and the scope of each, shows that limits are enforced in code where the tool is invoked (not in the prompt), and offers test results plus a sample action record that shows the scope applied.
evidence_that_satisfies: Per-agent inventory of tools and actions, with the systems and scopes each one can touch. | Enforcement in code at the tool-invocation layer (allowlists, parameter validation, scoped credentials), not only in the prompt. | Test results showing out-of-scope calls are blocked. | Per-action records that show which scope or permission applied.
not_enough_on_its_own: The model is instructed not to do X. | A workflow diagram with no enforcement point.
template_answer: The agent can call [N] tools: [list tool, target system and allowed operations, e.g. "issue_refund on the payment provider, up to EUR 200 per refund"]. Each call passes through [enforcement layer, e.g. a tool gateway] that checks [allowlist, parameter limits, scoped credential] before execution; calls outside scope are [blocked and logged / describe what happens]. We test this in [CI suite / quarterly test], last run [date], results attached. Each action record stores [the scope that applied] (sample attached).
references: FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-018; FINOS AIR AIR-SEC-024; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-019; CSA AICM IAM-19; CSA AICM AIS-11; CSA AICM IAM-05; NYDFS 500 500.7(a); NYDFS AI Letter Access controls; ISO 42001 A.9.4; DORA Art. 9(4); SIG AI domain; AIUC-1 B006; AIUC-1 D003.1; AIUC-1 A003; CSA AARM R1; CSA AARM R9; SOC 2 TSC CC6.1; SOC 2 TSC CC6.3

question: For every write in our systems, which identity performed it? Which agent and version, under which credential and scope, on whose behalf?
why_they_ask: Agents often act through shared service accounts or human-style browser logins, so the buyer's own logs cannot tell the agent from a staff member, and the vendor's logs cannot be matched to the buyer's.
strong_answer: Each agent deployment has its own non-human identity in the buyer's systems, credentials are kept away from the model, and every action record carries agent ID and version, credential ID, scope and the user, case or ticket it acted for, so the buyer's logs and the vendor's records can be joined.
evidence_that_satisfies: A distinct non-human identity per agent deployment, visible in the buyer's system logs. | Each action record carries agent ID and version, credential ID (never the secret), scope, and the initiating user, case or ticket. | Credentials isolated from the model and injected per call.
not_enough_on_its_own: A shared integration user for all agent traffic. | Identity known only inside the vendor's database.
template_answer: Agent actions in your [system] run under [a dedicated identity per deployment, name / a shared account: describe], which appears in your audit logs as [identity]. Every action record contains [agent ID, agent version, credential ID (never the secret), scope, initiating user / case / ticket ID]. Credentials are held in [vault / KMS] and [injected per call so the model never sees them / describe how exposure is limited]. A sample record joined to your system log is attached.
references: FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-023; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-021; FINOS AIR AIR-SEC-029; CSA AICM IAM-13; CSA AICM IAM-19; CSA AICM LOG-12; NYDFS 500 500.7(a); NYDFS 500 500.11(b)(1); AIUC-1 A003.2; AIUC-1 E015.2; CSA AARM R6; SOC 2 TSC CC6.2; SOC 2 TSC CC6.3

question: What stops prompt injection or a manipulated tool chain from causing the agent to take an action in our systems?
why_they_ask: Agents read untrusted content (emails, documents, web pages, tool outputs). If that content can steer a tool call, an attacker can act inside the buyer's systems through the agent.
strong_answer: Treats retrieved content as untrusted, filters inputs and outputs, validates tool choice and parameters before execution independently of the model, has red-team results that include indirect injection, and can detect unusual actions after the fact.
evidence_that_satisfies: Separation of instructions from untrusted data, plus input and output filtering. | Validation of tool selection and parameters before execution. | Red-team results that include indirect injection through retrieved content. | Detection of out-of-pattern actions in the action records.
not_enough_on_its_own: We use a safe model.
template_answer: Untrusted content ([emails, documents, web pages, tool outputs]) is kept separate from instructions by [method], and inputs and outputs are filtered by [method]. Before any tool call, [validator] checks tool choice and parameters against [policy]; [how you prevent the model from bypassing it, and how that is tested]. Our last red-team exercise on [date], by [internal team / third party], covered [direct and indirect injection]; a summary is attached. Unusual actions are flagged by [rule / monitor].
references: FINOS AIR AIR-SEC-025; FINOS AIR AIR-SEC-010; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-019; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-003; CSA AICM AIS-15; CSA AICM AIS-08 / AIS-09; CSA AICM MDS-06 / MDS-07; NIST AI 600-1 MS-2.7-007; NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.7; EU AI Act Art. 15(5); AIUC-1 B002; AIUC-1 B005; CSA AARM R3

question: For any single agent action, can you produce the complete record? What triggered it, which inputs and sources it used, the exact tool call and arguments, the system's response, and the downstream effect.
why_they_ask: Reviewers and examiners pick one case and ask you to walk through it. If the record is spread across chat transcripts, APM traces and the vendor UI, the answer takes days and cannot be checked.
strong_answer: Can pick any action and produce, in minutes, one record with trigger, inputs and sources, exact tool call and arguments, the system's response, timestamps and trace ID, with sensitive fields redacted.
evidence_that_satisfies: A per-action record with trigger, inputs, retrieved sources, tool name, arguments (redacted where needed), the system response, timestamps and a trace ID. | A sample export for one real (redacted) case, produced on request in minutes.
not_enough_on_its_own: A chat transcript without the tool calls. | Infrastructure logs only.
template_answer: Every action produces one record containing: trigger ([event / user request]), inputs and retrieved sources, tool name and arguments (with [fields] redacted), the target system's response, timestamps and trace ID. We can export the full record for any action or case within [time]. A redacted example for one real case is attached.
references: FINOS AIR AIR-DET-021; CSA AICM LOG-11; CSA AICM LOG-08; CSA AICM LOG-14 / LOG-15; EU AI Act Art. 12(1)-(2); ISO 42001 A.6.2.8; NYDFS 500 500.6(a)(1); NAIC AI Bulletin Sec. 3, 3.3(b)-(c); NYDFS CL7 ¶19; AIUC-1 E015; AIUC-1 E015.2; AIUC-1 D003.3; CSA AARM R5; SOC 2 TSC PI1.3

question: Which model and version handled a given action, including actions served by versions you have since retired?
why_they_ask: Vendors route between several models and providers. When a past decision is challenged, the buyer must know which model produced it, even if that model is gone.
strong_answer: Stores the provider, model name and pinned version on every action record, and keeps an inventory of retired versions with the dates they were in use.
evidence_that_satisfies: Model provider, model name and pinned version stored on every action record. | A model inventory that keeps retired versions with their active dates.
not_enough_on_its_own: A current list of providers with no per-action version.
template_answer: Each action record stores model provider, model name and pinned version, e.g. [example]. We keep a model inventory including retired versions and their active dates ([link / attachment]), so any past action can be matched to the model that handled it.
references: FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-010; FINOS AIR AIR-OP-005; NIST AI 600-1 GV-1.6-003; NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.6 / 1.7; NAIC AI Bulletin Sec. 3, 3.3(a); NYDFS CL7 ¶29; CSA AICM MDS-03 to MDS-05; CSA AICM MDS-09

question: Show every model endpoint and external service the agent actually called for our traffic, not just the list in your inventory.
why_they_ask: An inventory says what should be called. Destination records show what was called, which is what data-flow and data-residency reviews need.
strong_answer: Records each outbound call per action (provider, endpoint, region) and periodically compares actual destinations with the declared sub-processor list for that buyer.
evidence_that_satisfies: Per-action record of each outbound call (provider, endpoint, region). | A periodic summary per buyer comparing actual destinations with the declared sub-processor list.
not_enough_on_its_own: A static sub-processor page.
template_answer: Each action record lists the outbound calls made: [provider, endpoint, region]. Every [month / quarter] we compare actual destinations for your traffic with the declared sub-processor list and share the result. The latest comparison is attached.
references: CSA AICM STA-16; CSA AICM DSP-05; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-004; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-020; NYDFS AI Letter Monitoring; DORA Art. 30(2)(b); AIUC-1 E009

question: Which documents and records contributed to each answer or action?
why_they_ask: Reviewers need to trace an output back to its sources, both to check correctness and to confirm the agent only used data it was entitled to see.
strong_answer: Stores the ID and version of each document or record the agent used, and retrieval respects the access controls of the source system.
evidence_that_satisfies: Source IDs (document, record, version) stored on the action record. | Entitlement checks that carry the source system's access controls into retrieval.
not_enough_on_its_own: Citations shown in the UI but not retained.
template_answer: For each answer or action we store the IDs and versions of the sources used ([document IDs, record IDs]). Retrieval runs under [the requesting user's permissions / a scoped identity], so the agent only sees what [that user / that scope] is entitled to. An example record with sources is attached.
references: FINOS AIR AIR-DET-013; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-016; CSA AICM DSP-20; ISO 42001 A.7.5

question: What is the lineage of the data used in a decision? Where did each input come from, and how current was it?
why_they_ask: Insurance and lending regulators ask for data lineage, and stale or wrong inputs are a common root cause of bad decisions.
strong_answer: Documents data flows per use case and stores, with each decision, where every input came from and when it was retrieved.
evidence_that_satisfies: Documented data flows per use case. | Input source and retrieval timestamp stored with the decision.
not_enough_on_its_own: A generic architecture diagram.
template_answer: For [use case], inputs come from [sources]. A data-flow diagram is attached. With each decision we store the source and retrieval time of every input, so you can see how current the data was at the time.
references: NAIC AI Bulletin Sec. 3, 3.2; NYDFS CL7 ¶29; ISO 42001 A.7.5; CSA AICM DSP-20; NIST AI 600-1 GV-6.1-008

question: For an adverse decision, can you give the specific reasons and the data relied on? A proprietary model is not an acceptable reason to withhold them.
why_they_ask: Consumer-facing lenders and insurers must give specific reasons for adverse outcomes, and regulators reject vendor secrecy as an excuse.
strong_answer: Stores reason codes and the specific inputs relied on for each decision, and can produce an explanation for a specific adverse outcome from that record.
evidence_that_satisfies: Reason codes and the specific inputs relied on, stored per decision. | A sample adverse-decision explanation produced from the stored record.
not_enough_on_its_own: Global feature importance for the model.
template_answer: For each decision we store reason codes ([list or link]) and the specific inputs relied on. An explanation for an individual adverse outcome is generated from that stored record, not reconstructed later. A redacted sample is attached.
references: NYDFS CL7 ¶39-¶40; NYDFS CL7 ¶44; EU AI Act Art. 86(1); NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.9; CSA AICM GRC-13 / GRC-14; FINOS AIR AIR-OP-017

question: For customer-facing agents, can you show per interaction that the conduct rules for our use case were met, such as AI disclosure, contact-time windows and contact-frequency limits?
why_they_ask: In collections, servicing and sales, a single non-compliant contact can be a violation. Buyers want per-interaction proof, not a policy that the platform enforces rules.
strong_answer: Records, per interaction, the disclosure given, the local time of contact, the contact count at that moment and the rule version applied, so compliance can be shown for any single contact.
evidence_that_satisfies: Per-interaction record of the disclosure given, the time in the customer's time zone, and the frequency counter at the time of contact. | Rule configuration and version applied to each interaction.
not_enough_on_its_own: QA reviews a sample of calls.
template_answer: For each interaction we record the AI disclosure given ([wording]), the time in the customer's time zone, the contact-frequency count at that moment, and the version of the rule set applied ([rule set]). An export for a sample of [N] interactions is attached.
references: EU AI Act Art. 50(1); CSA AICM LOG-11; AIUC-1 E016

question: When the agent says it did something, how do you know it actually happened in our system, as described?
why_they_ask: An agent's own summary ("refund issued") is not evidence. Agents can report success while the target system shows an error, a different amount or nothing at all. Reviewers want the system of record's response next to the claim.
strong_answer: Stores the agent's claim next to the target system's actual response, optionally reads the object back from the system of record to confirm, and reports the mismatch rate to the buyer.
evidence_that_satisfies: Each action record stores both the agent's claim and the target system's actual response (status, object ID, returned values). | Optional read-back that queries the system of record and records match or mismatch. | Mismatch rate per period, reported to the buyer.
not_enough_on_its_own: The agent's final message. | HTTP 200 without checking the returned object.
template_answer: Each action record stores both what the agent reported and the response from [target system] (status, object ID, returned values). For [high-impact actions, e.g. refunds] we also read the object back from [system] and record match or mismatch. The mismatch rate for [period] was [x] ([report attached]).
references: FINOS AIR AIR-DET-021; NYDFS 500 500.6(a)(1); EU AI Act Art. 12(2); NAIC AI Bulletin Sec. 3, 3.4; NIST AI RMF MEASURE 2.4; AIUC-1 E015.2; CSA AARM R5; SOC 2 TSC PI1.4

question: How do you detect and report actions that failed, only partly completed, or produced a different result than intended?
why_they_ask: Silent failures are the hardest to catch. A buyer wants to see failures counted and reported, not discovered by a customer.
strong_answer: Counts failed, partial and mismatched actions per period with examples, has alert thresholds and owners, and reconciles high-impact actions against the system of record.
evidence_that_satisfies: Failed, partial and mismatched actions counted per period, with examples, in the buyer's report. | Alert thresholds and owners. | Reconciliation against the system of record for high-impact actions.
not_enough_on_its_own: Error rate from APM only.
template_answer: Failed, partial and mismatched actions are counted and included in your [monthly] report with examples. Alerts fire at [threshold] and go to [owner]. For [action types] we reconcile against [system] every [period]. The last report is attached.
references: CSA AICM LOG-13; CSA AICM MDS-11; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-004; NIST AI 600-1 MG-4.3-002; ISO 42001 A.6.2.6; DORA Art. 17(1)-(3); SOC 2 TSC PI1.3; SOC 2 TSC CC7.2

question: Are agent action records protected so that any edit, deletion, reordering or truncation after the fact is detectable?
why_they_ask: Access controls protect logs from outsiders, not from the party that writes them. "Immutable" is a claim; reviewers increasingly ask for the mechanism.
strong_answer: Names the mechanism: hash-chained, signed records with keys separated from operators, periodic commitments (for example Merkle roots) so edits, deletions, reordering and truncation are all detectable, and synchronized clocks.
evidence_that_satisfies: Hash-chained, append-only records (each record commits to the previous one). | Digital signatures with keys separated from application operators. | Periodic commitment of segment digests (for example a Merkle root) so truncation is detectable. | Synchronized clocks and documented key management.
not_enough_on_its_own: "Logs are immutable" with no mechanism. | Write-protected storage alone, where the vendor still controls the storage.
template_answer: Action records are [append-only and hash-chained, each record including the hash of the previous one / describe]. Records are signed with [algorithm] keys held in [KMS / HSM], [separate from the people who run the agent / describe]. Every [period] we commit a digest of the latest records [to an external log / to you], so [truncation is also detectable / describe]. Clocks are synchronized via [time source]. Key management is documented in [document].
references: FINOS AIR AIR-DET-021; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-024; DORA RTS 2024/1774 Art. 12; CSA AICM LOG-09; CSA AICM IAM-12; CSA AICM LOG-02; CSA AICM LOG-06; NIST AI 600-1 MS-2.8-003; NYDFS 500 500.6(a); AIUC-1 E015.4; CSA AARM R5; CSA AARM R2; SOC 2 TSC PI1.5

question: Can we, our auditor or our regulator verify those records ourselves, without access to your systems and without relying on your word?
why_they_ask: Logs the vendor writes, stores and attests to are self-reported evidence. The strongest records are those a third party can check independently.
strong_answer: Gives the buyer an exported bundle and a verification tool they run themselves, offline, with documented public keys and digests anchored outside the vendor, plus a demo of a tampered bundle failing.
evidence_that_satisfies: A verification tool the buyer can run offline on an exported bundle. | Public keys and verification steps documented. | Record digests anchored outside the vendor (for example an append-only transparency log) or held by the buyer. | A worked example showing a tampered bundle failing verification.
not_enough_on_its_own: A screenshot or PDF export from the vendor's UI. | A SOC 2 report, which covers controls, not individual records.
template_answer: To verify records yourself, you [run verifier, e.g. an open-source CLI, offline against an exported bundle / describe current process] using our published public key [key ID]. Segment digests are anchored in [external log / your storage], so [what a rewrite of history would show, and to whom]. A sample bundle, the verification steps and a tampered example that fails are attached.
references: FINOS AIR AIR-DET-021; DORA Art. 30(3)(e); EU AI Act Art. 13(3)(f); AIUC-1 E015.4; CSA AARM R5

question: Who at your company can read, change or delete agent records, and is that access itself logged?
why_they_ask: Privileged insiders are the main threat to record integrity. Reviewers expect named roles and an access trail.
strong_answer: Lists the named roles with access to record storage and signing keys, logs each access against an individual identity, and separates people who run the agent from people who can touch records or keys.
evidence_that_satisfies: Named roles with access to record storage and keys. | Access to records logged against individual identities and reviewed. | Separation between people who run the agent and people who can touch records or keys.
not_enough_on_its_own: "Only engineers have access."
template_answer: Access to record storage is limited to [roles, number of people]; access to signing keys to [roles]. Every access is [logged against an individual identity and reviewed every period / describe]. People who operate the agent [cannot change records or keys / describe the separation]. The latest access review is attached.
references: CSA AICM LOG-04; CSA AICM IAM-12; CSA AICM IAM-04; NYDFS 500 500.7(c); AIUC-1 E015.3; SOC 2 TSC CC6.3

question: After an incident, can you reconstruct exactly what the agent did, in which of our systems, under which identity, and in what order?
why_they_ask: Incident response, root-cause analysis and regulator notifications all depend on an ordered, complete account. Gaps are what turn an incident into a finding.
strong_answer: Can export, for any time window or case, an ordered account of every action across the buyer's systems, with evidence that the sequence is complete and unaltered, and knows from a test how long that takes.
evidence_that_satisfies: For a time window or case, an ordered export of all actions across all buyer systems, with identity, scope, inputs and system responses. | Evidence the sequence is complete (no gaps) and unaltered. | A tabletop exercise or test showing how long reconstruction takes.
not_enough_on_its_own: Our engineers can query the database.
template_answer: For any time window or case we can export [every agent action across systems], in order, with [identity, scope, inputs and system responses]. [Mechanism, e.g. a hash chain plus externally committed digests] shows the exported sequence has not been altered or cut short. In our last tabletop on [date], a full reconstruction took [time].
references: FINOS AIR AIR-DET-021; NYDFS 500 500.6(a); NYDFS 500 500.16(a)(1); DORA Art. 17(1)-(3); DORA Art. 30(2)(f); EU AI Act Art. 73; CSA AICM SEF-09; CSA AICM LOG-05 / LOG-06; NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4.3; AIUC-1 E015; AIUC-1 E001; CSA AARM R5 / R6; SOC 2 TSC CC7.4

question: How do you detect and report model failures, data leakage or harmful outputs, and on what timeline will we hear about them?
why_they_ask: The buyer has its own notification clocks (72 hours under NYDFS 500, 4 hours from classification and at most 24 hours from awareness under DORA). Vendor timelines must fit inside them.
strong_answer: Commits in the contract to a notification timeline that fits inside the buyer's own regulatory clocks, names the detection sources and owners, and can show a recent incident or tabletop record.
evidence_that_satisfies: Contractual notification timeline that fits the buyer's obligations. | Detection sources (monitoring, alerts, user reports) and owners. | A recent incident report or tabletop record (redacted).
not_enough_on_its_own: A generic incident-response policy with no AI-specific triggers.
template_answer: We detect [model failures, data leakage, harmful outputs] through [monitoring, alerts, user reports], owned by [team]. We notify you within [hours] of detection, as set out in [contract clause], which fits within [your NYDFS / DORA timelines]. A redacted incident or tabletop report from [date] is attached.
references: NYDFS 500 500.11(b)(3); NYDFS 500 500.17(a); NYDFS AI Letter Risk assessments; DORA Art. 19; RTS 2025/301; EU AI Act Art. 73(2)-(6); CSA AICM SEF-07; CSA AICM MDS-11; ISO 42001 A.8.4; NIST AI 600-1 MG-4.3-002; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-001; FS-ISAC GenAI Levels 2-3; AIUC-1 E001; AIUC-1 E002; SOC 2 TSC CC7.3; SOC 2 TSC CC2.3

question: How quickly can we stop the agent, or roll it back to a previous model or configuration?
why_they_ask: When something goes wrong the first question is how to stop it. Rollback also matters when a provider changes a model underneath you.
strong_answer: Gives the buyer a kill switch it can trigger itself with a tested time to effect, and a documented rollback path to a pinned earlier model, prompt and configuration.
evidence_that_satisfies: A kill switch the buyer can trigger, with tested time to effect. | Pinned model and prompt versions with a documented rollback path. | Results of the last rollback test.
not_enough_on_its_own: Contact support.
template_answer: You can stop the agent yourself via [console button / API / revoking credential], taking effect within [time] (tested [date]). Model, prompt and configuration versions are pinned, and we can roll back to [previous version] within [time]. Results of the last stop and rollback test are attached.
references: EU AI Act Art. 14(4)(e); NIST AI RMF MANAGE 2.4; NIST AI 600-1 MG-2.4-002 / MG-2.4-004; CSA AICM CCC-09; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-010; ISO 42001 A.6.2.5; DORA Art. 28(7)-(8); Art. 30(3)(f); NYDFS 500 500.16(a); SOC 2 TSC CC7.5

question: What do you log about agent activity, how long do you keep it, who can access it, and can you export it to our SIEM or GRC tool?
why_they_ask: Log management is an explicit topic in the deepest tier of bank AI due diligence. Short default retention is a common finding.
strong_answer: Lists the agent-level events logged (not just infrastructure), the retention per log type, who can access them, and offers an export into the buyer's SIEM or GRC tool with a sample.
evidence_that_satisfies: A list of logged event types for agent actions (not just infrastructure). | Retention period per log type. | Export mechanism (API or scheduled delivery) and a sample export.
not_enough_on_its_own: "Logs retained for 30 days" with no agent-action logs.
template_answer: We log [event types: actions, tool calls, outcomes, reviews, config changes]. Retention: [period per type]. Access: [roles]. You can receive records via [API / scheduled delivery / your SIEM or object storage] in [format]. A sample export is attached.
references: FS-ISAC GenAI Level 3; CSA AICM LOG-01 / LOG-02 / LOG-07; DORA RTS 2024/1774 Art. 12; ISO 42001 A.6.2.8; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-004; NYDFS AI Letter Monitoring; SIG AI domain; AIUC-1 E015.3; CSA AARM R8; SOC 2 TSC CC7.2

question: Can we hold our own copy of the agent's event logs for the period our rules require?
why_they_ask: Under the EU AI Act, deployers of high-risk systems must keep the logs that are under their control for at least six months, and financial institutions keep them under their financial-services record rules. A buyer-held copy is how a deployer shows it meets that, rather than depending on the vendor.
strong_answer: Delivers records continuously or on a schedule into storage the buyer controls, in a documented format that stays verifiable without the vendor.
evidence_that_satisfies: Continuous or scheduled delivery of records into storage the buyer controls. | Format documented so the buyer's copy remains verifiable on its own.
not_enough_on_its_own: We can send logs on request.
template_answer: Records are delivered [continuously / every period] to [your bucket / SIEM / storage], which you control. The format is documented ([link]) and each copy can be verified on its own, without access to our systems. You set retention there to match your rules.
references: EU AI Act Art. 26(6); EU AI Act Art. 19(1)-(2); EU AI Act Art. 12(1); NYDFS 500 500.6(b); CSA AARM Sec. VI.D

question: How do we get timely access to our data and to reports on the agent's activity, by type and frequency?
why_they_ask: Buyers must be able to monitor the service and to give data to auditors and regulators on demand.
strong_answer: Names the report types and cadence in the contract and lets the buyer export its own data and records without a support ticket.
evidence_that_satisfies: Report types and cadence in the contract (activity, failures, incidents, changes). | Self-service export of the buyer's data and records.
not_enough_on_its_own: A dashboard with no export.
template_answer: You receive [activity, failure, incident and change] reports every [period], as defined in [contract section]. You can export your data and agent records at any time via [self-service export / API].
references: DORA Art. 30(2)(d); DORA RTS 2024/1773 Art. 3; EU AI Act Art. 13(3)(f); ISO 42001 A.8.5; NAIC AI Bulletin Sec. 4, 1.1-1.3

question: Does the retention of agent records match our own record-keeping obligations, and what happens to the records when the contract ends?
why_they_ask: Vendor defaults (often weeks) rarely match the buyer's retention duties (often years). On exit, the buyer still needs the records.
strong_answer: Lets each buyer set retention to its own obligations and commits, on exit, to return records in a verifiable format before deleting them.
evidence_that_satisfies: Retention configurable per buyer, set to the buyer's requirement. | Exit clause covering return of records in a verifiable format before deletion.
not_enough_on_its_own: A fixed vendor-wide retention period.
template_answer: Retention is configurable per customer; for you it is set to [period] to match [your obligation]. On termination we return all records in [format], verifiable without us, within [days], and delete our copies after your confirmation, per [contract clause].
references: NYDFS 500 500.6(b); EU AI Act Art. 19(2); Art. 26(6); DORA Art. 28(8); Art. 30(2)(d); NAIC AI Bulletin Sec. 3, 3.6; SOC 2 TSC C1.2

question: Which foundation models and providers sit behind each feature, and how will you notify us when they change?
why_they_ask: The model is the most important sub-component. Silent model swaps change behaviour and can invalidate the buyer's validation.
strong_answer: Lists models and providers per feature with versions, commits contractually to advance notice of changes, and keeps a change log the buyer can see.
evidence_that_satisfies: Model and provider list per feature, with versions. | Contractual advance notice of model or provider changes. | Change log available to the buyer.
not_enough_on_its_own: We use leading LLMs.
template_answer: [Feature]: [provider, model, version]. [Feature]: [provider, model, version]. We give [N days] advance notice of any model or provider change, per [contract clause]. The change log is at [link].
references: FS-ISAC GenAI Level 1; NIST AI 600-1 GV-1.6-003; GV-6.2-007; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-007; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-010; CSA AICM CCC-05; STA-08; STA-16; NYDFS AI Letter Data management; DORA Art. 28(3); ISO 42001 A.4.4; A.10.3; SOC 2 TSC CC3.4

question: How are changes to prompts, agent logic, tools and models tested, approved and versioned before they reach our traffic?
why_they_ask: For agents, a prompt edit is a code change. Buyers want the same change control they expect for software.
strong_answer: Versions prompts, tools and configs like code, runs evaluations before release with a named approver, stores the version on every action record, and gives the buyer a change history it can review.
evidence_that_satisfies: Versioned prompts, tool definitions and configs, with the version stored on each action record. | Pre-release evaluation results and a named approver per change. | Change history the buyer can review.
not_enough_on_its_own: Prompts edited in a vendor console with no history.
template_answer: Prompts, tool definitions and configs are versioned in [repository]. Every change runs [evaluation suite] and needs approval from [role] before release. The active version is stored on each action record. Change history for your deployment is available at [link].

question: How is the agent validated, independently or on an ongoing basis, including drift and bias testing?
why_they_ask: Banks and insurers apply model risk management to vendor models. They need validation evidence they can file.
strong_answer: Shares the validation method and latest results (including bias testing where consumers are affected), drift monitoring with re-validation triggers, and any independent validation report.
evidence_that_satisfies: Validation methodology and latest results, including bias testing where decisions affect consumers. | Drift monitoring and re-validation triggers. | Any independent validation report.
not_enough_on_its_own: Marketing benchmark numbers.
template_answer: We validate [agent / model] using [method]; latest results from [date] are attached, including bias testing on [dimensions] where decisions affect consumers. Drift is monitored by [metric]; re-validation is triggered by [condition]. [Independent validation by X on date / none yet].

question: What ongoing monitoring do you report to us? Performance, error rates, complaints and drift.
why_they_ask: Third-party oversight is continuous, not a one-time review. The buyer needs regular data to show its own supervisors.
strong_answer: Sends a recurring report with defined metrics and thresholds (performance, errors, complaints, drift) and escalates when a threshold is breached.
evidence_that_satisfies: A recurring report with defined metrics and thresholds. | Escalation when thresholds are breached.
not_enough_on_its_own: Ad-hoc updates on request.
template_answer: Every [period] you receive a report covering [performance, error rate, mismatch rate, complaints, drift] against agreed thresholds. Breaches are escalated to [contact] within [time]. A sample report is attached.
references: NIST AI RMF GOVERN 1.5; MEASURE 2.4; MANAGE 4.1; EU AI Act Art. 72; ISO 42001 A.6.2.6; CSA AICM MDS-10; DORA Art. 30(3)(a); NYDFS CL7 ¶29-¶30; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-011; AIUC-1 C008

question: Is our data used to train or improve any model? How long are prompts, uploads and outputs kept, and how is deletion verified?
why_they_ask: The first AI question in almost every questionnaire. Buyers also check that the vendor's model providers make the same commitment.
strong_answer: States in the contract that buyer data is not used for training, by the vendor or its model providers, gives the retention per data type, and confirms deletion on request.
evidence_that_satisfies: Contract terms on no training and on retention, including for model providers (zero retention where available). | Retention schedule per data type. | Deletion procedure and a deletion confirmation on request.
not_enough_on_its_own: A privacy policy page.
template_answer: Your data [is not used / is used, under these conditions:] to train or improve any model, by us or by [providers], per [contract clause / provider terms]. Retention: prompts [period], uploads [period], outputs [period]; [zero-retention terms with providers where available]. Deletion follows [procedure], and we [confirm it in writing on request].

question: What personal or confidential data ends up inside your agent action records, and how is it minimized, redacted or protected?
why_they_ask: Detailed action records are a second copy of customer data. Reviewers will ask the same data questions about the records as about the product.
strong_answer: Redacts or hashes sensitive fields before records are stored, documents the data classes per record field, and applies the same access and retention rules to records as to the product.
evidence_that_satisfies: Field-level redaction or hashing of sensitive arguments before records are stored. | Documented data classes per record field. | Access and retention rules for records match the data policy.
not_enough_on_its_own: Full request and response bodies logged by default.
template_answer: Before a record is stored, [fields, e.g. card numbers, account numbers] are [redacted / hashed]. The data classes per record field are documented in [document]. Records follow the same access and retention rules as your other data with us.
references: NYDFS AI Letter Data management; FINOS AIR AIR-PREV-014; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-001; CSA AICM DSP-12; DORA Art. 30(2)(c); AIUC-1 A006; AIUC-1 E015.3; SOC 2 TSC C1.1

group: Human oversight (as the buyer defines it)
question: Under the oversight model we define for this use case, which agent actions need human review, and can you show that the review happened whenever it was required?
why_they_ask: The buyer chooses how much oversight a use case needs (by risk, amount, customer impact). What it needs from the vendor is evidence that its chosen model was followed, including that review came before execution where the buyer requires that.
strong_answer: Expresses the buyer's oversight rules as readable configuration, records per action whether review applied, who reviewed, the decision and its timing relative to execution, and reports exceptions.
evidence_that_satisfies: Oversight rules expressed as configuration the buyer can read and change. | Per-action record showing whether review applied, who reviewed, the decision, and its timing relative to execution. | An exceptions report for actions that should have been reviewed but were not.
not_enough_on_its_own: A workflow screenshot. | A statement that "humans are in the loop".
template_answer: Your oversight rules are configured as [rules, e.g. review for refunds above EUR X], visible and editable by you in [place]. For each action the record shows whether review applied, who reviewed, the decision, and the time of review relative to execution. Actions that should have been reviewed but were not appear in [exceptions report].

group: Human oversight (as the buyer defines it)
question: What audit trail exists when a person overrides, corrects or reverses what the agent did or recommended?
why_they_ask: Overrides show where the agent is wrong and who took responsibility. Both matter in a dispute.
strong_answer: Links each override to the original action with who, when, what changed and why, and reports override rates over time.
evidence_that_satisfies: Override records linked to the original action, with who, when, what changed and why. | Override rates reported over time.
not_enough_on_its_own: Overrides visible only as a later edit in the target system.
template_answer: When someone overrides, corrects or reverses an agent action, we record who, when, what changed and why, linked to the original action record. Override rates are included in your [period] report.
references: NIST AI RMF MANAGE 4.1; MEASURE 3.3; EU AI Act Art. 14(4)(d); CSA AICM IAM-18; FINOS AIR AIR-DET-011; AIUC-1 C009

question: Which model, voice, speech-to-text, text-to-speech and tool providers are involved, and what are their data retention and training terms?
why_they_ask: Nth-party risk is its own category in bank AI due diligence. Each provider is another place customer data can go.
strong_answer: Publishes a complete sub-processor list that includes AI, voice and tool providers with region and purpose, with each provider's retention and training terms, and a change notice process.
evidence_that_satisfies: Complete sub-processor list including AI providers, with region and purpose. | Each provider's retention and training terms. | Notice process for sub-processor changes.
not_enough_on_its_own: "No subprocessors available."
template_answer: Sub-processors involved in the agent: [provider, purpose, region, retention, training terms] for each of model, speech-to-text, text-to-speech and tools. The full list is at [link]. We notify you [N days] before adding or changing one.

question: What audit rights or audit reports cover the AI system itself, not just your infrastructure?
why_they_ask: Insurers and banks are expected to secure audit rights over third-party AI. A SOC 2 report usually covers infrastructure and access, not agent behaviour.
strong_answer: Grants audit rights that cover the AI system itself and provides reports whose scope includes agent behaviour, together with record samples the buyer can verify.
evidence_that_satisfies: Audit-rights clause covering the AI system. | Reports whose scope includes agent behaviour, plus record samples the buyer can verify.
not_enough_on_its_own: A SOC 2 report alone.
template_answer: [Contract clause] gives you audit rights over the AI system, including [model use, agent actions, records]. Our [SOC 2 Type II / other report] covers [scope]. For agent behaviour we provide verifiable record samples for any period you choose.

question: Will you cooperate with regulatory inquiries and give examiners access to the documentation and records they ask for?
why_they_ask: Regulators examine the buyer, and through the buyer, its AI vendors. Buyers need the cooperation in writing and the artifacts ready.
strong_answer: Commits in writing to cooperate with regulators and keeps an evidence package ready: model documentation, validation, change history and verifiable action records.
evidence_that_satisfies: Regulatory cooperation clause. | A ready evidence package: model documentation, validation, change history and verifiable action records.
not_enough_on_its_own: Best-effort cooperation with no artifacts.
template_answer: [Contract clause] commits us to cooperate with your regulators and to give examiners access to documentation and records. We keep an evidence package ready: model documentation, validation results, change history and verifiable action records, deliverable within [time].
